title: Finite cohomology below a pseudo-coherent bound
statement: Let R be a commutative ring with identity (including the zero ring, as in the Stacks conventions) and m an integer. Let D(R) be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of R-modules. Call an object C of D(R) m-pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-m-pseudo-coherent] if there are a bounded complex E^\bullet of finite free R-modules and a morphism E^\bullet\to C in D(R) inducing isomorphisms H^i(E^\bullet)\to H^i(C) for i>m and a surjection H^m(E^\bullet)\to H^m(C). If K^\bullet is a complex of R-modules, viewed as an object of D(R), which is m-pseudo-coherent and satisfies H^i(K^\bullet)=0 for every i>m, then H^m(K^\bullet) is a finite type R-module.

proof.text: Unpack the m-pseudo-coherent witness E, its upper bound b, its degreewise finite free modules, and f:Q(E)→Q(K). A free module is projective (Mathlib ModuleCat.projective_of_categoryTheory_projective). For i>m, the isomorphism H^i(f) and H^i(K)=0 give H^i(Q(E))=0; homologyFunctorFactors identifies this with E.homology i, so E is exact at i.

Set B=max(m,b), so E is strictly supported in degrees ≤B. Descend from B to m, proving that Z^i(E) is a retract of E^i. At B the outgoing differential is zero, so iCyclesIso identifies the cycles with E^B. In the induction step n>m, Z^n(E) is projective as a retract of E^n (Retract.projective). Exactness at n makes g:E^(n-1)→Z^n(E) an epimorphism (ShortComplex.Exact.epi_toCycles, transported by cyclesIsoSc'). Let s:Z^n(E)→E^(n-1) be a section supplied by Projective.factorThru. The endomorphism 1-g≫s of E^(n-1) has zero composite with d^(n-1), so liftCycles factors it through Z^(n-1)(E). Its restriction to Z^(n-1)(E) is the identity, because iCycles≫g=0. This is the required retract. The induction is Int.leInductionDown, with invariant m≤i→Nonempty(Retract(Z^i(E),E^i)). This is the cycle-level form of the source's split top-term cancellation; no modified complex or freeness of a kernel is required.

At i=m, the retract projection E^m→Z^m(E) is epic and hence surjective by ModuleCat.epi_iff_surjective. Apply Module.Finite.of_surjective to obtain finite cycles, then to homologyπ to obtain finite H^m(E). Transport finite generation to H^m(Q(E)) using the inverse of homologyFunctorFactors, and apply Module.Finite.of_surjective again to H^m(f), which is epic by the witness hypothesis. This proves finite generation of H^m(Q(K)).
